title: Small area estimation of tree diameter distributions under a multivariate compositional Fay–Herriot model
content:
Abstract
Accurate estimation of tree diameter distributions is essential for sustainable forest management but remains challenging when most forest management units (FMUs) contain only a few sample plots. Standard parametric models (e.g. Weibull) require large within-unit samples or many tens to hundreds of trees per stand to achieve reliable fits and therefore perform poorly in data-sparse inventories. We extend the area-level multivariate Fay–Herriot model to a trivariate compositional mixed model (TriCompFH) for small-area estimation of tree diameter-class distributions. The new methodology (i) applies an additive log-ratio transformation to satisfy the unit-sum constraint of compositional data, (ii) jointly models three diameter at breast height (DBH)–class proportions while deriving the fourth as the complement, and (iii) integrates auxiliary canopy-height metrics from WorldView-2 imagery with historical census data. Random effects are estimated via residual maximum likelihood, and uncertainty is quantified using a parametric bootstrap. TriCompFH was applied to clustered FMUs in a heterogeneous uneven-aged fir forest dominated by Abies borisii-regis Mattf. Model diagnostics confirmed normality and homoscedasticity, and comparisons with design-based estimators showed close agreement on average. TriCompFH reduced relative uncertainty by 68%–77% across the three modelled DBH classes, with per-small-area coefficients of variation <5% in the majority of the small areas—a substantial improvement over direct estimators. Beyond class proportions, TriCompFH provides stem densities and stand indices (stand density index, relative density index, q-ratios, recruitment efficiency index), reproducing the inverse J-shaped structure typical of uneven-aged forests while highlighting recruitment bottlenecks and over-stocked domains. TriCompFH delivers reliable DBH-class estimates for data-sparse inventories, enabling informed, density-based management decisions.
